subject: setting some widths and browser/OS compatibility

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: setting some widths and browser/OS compatibility
parts:
Hello, 

This is surely an html question rather than a shiny question. 

 I have set some widths in a shiny app, for example like this for the sidebar:

                     sidebarPanel(
                       style="min-width:235px;max-width:375px", 

and similarly for some wellPanels. 

The rendering is perfect (the first goal is to handle the behavior when the user plays with size of the browser windows) on my Linux machine with a 17inches screen, but it is bad on my Windows machine with a 15inches screen.

I don't know whether this is due to the OS or the size screen. I'd like to know what is the good way to set the widths ?

messages.author: e6d426c9552b1af9
messages.subject: Re: setting some widths and browser/OS compatibility
parts:
Hi,

You can use specific bootstrap classes that will render your application differently depending on the device used. See the Shiny layout guide for some suggestions on this.

Alternatively, you can use jQuery to obtain height and width information and use this to set specific width variables. In jQuery these are available via $(window).width() etc, see here. Then instead of expressing variables in a fixed number of pixels, you express them as a function of the width info obtained via jQuery. This would require you to add some javascript to your code, which may unnecessarily complicate your code.

An advantage of the bootstrap classes is that they automatically do the computations for you, however, you may have less control over what you want to do precisely.
 
caveat: I'm definitely not an expert in HTML5/CSS, so take my suggestions with a pinch of salt please ;-)
